_about: Public-domain William Staughton (1770-1829), Baptist minister in Philadelphia and first president of Columbian College, for the Word Hoard: his sermons and discourses of 1797 to 1826. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-24 by lane A, round 135 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

staughton-drowning-1797: A discourse occasioned by the sudden death of three young persons by drowning ...  1797 (catalogued 1797)
staughton-missionary-encouragement: Missionary-encouragement : a discourse, delivered on Wednesday evening, the 16th of May, 1798, before the Philadelphia Missionary Society and the congregation of the Baptist Meeting House, Philadelphia / by the Rev. William Staughton (Philadelphia : Printed by Stephen C. Ustick, 1798)
staughton-compassion-poor: Compassion to the poor recommended : a sermon delivered in the First Baptist Meeting House, Philadelphia, February fourth, 1810 (Philadelphia : Printed by Bartholomew Graves, 1810)
staughton-servant-of-god: The Servant of God Concluding his Labours.  1814-05 (catalogued 1814)
staughton-capitol-1826: Sermon, delivered in the Capitol of the United States; on Lord's day, July 16, 1826; at the request of the citizens of Washington, on the death of Mr. Jefferson and Mr. Adams (Washington, Columbian office, 1826)
